Class ParquetSerializer

Namespace
ParquetNeo.Serialization
Assembly
ParquetNeo.Serialization.dll

Writes objects as rows of a Parquet file (Serialize<TRow>(IEnumerable<TRow>, Stream, ParquetSerializerOptions?) and SerializeAsync<TRow>(IEnumerable<TRow>, Stream, ParquetSerializerOptions?, CancellationToken)), and reads rows back (Deserialize<TRow>(Stream, ParquetDeserializerOptions?), DeserializeAll<TRow>(Stream, ParquetDeserializerOptions?) and their asynchronous forms; see the remarks below for what reading supports). Each public property becomes a column, named after the property and typed by the convention below, which attributes on the property adjust: ParquetColumnAttribute, ParquetIgnoreAttribute, ParquetDecimalAttribute, ParquetTimestampAttribute, ParquetTimeAttribute and ParquetEncodingAttribute.

Remarks

A column is optional (it can hold nulls) when the property is a Nullable<T>, or a reference type that is not declared non-nullable (nullable reference types decide, including for the elements of collections and the values of dictionaries). Writing a null where the column is required is an ArgumentException that names the property and the row.

Supported types: bool, the integers of every width, float, double, Half, decimal (precision 38 and scale 18 unless set), string, byte arrays, Guid, DateTime and DateTimeOffset (UTC microseconds unless set), DateOnly and TimeOnly (microseconds unless set), and enums (written by name, annotated ENUM). Beyond those:

  • an object (a class, record or struct with public properties) is a group of the columns of its own properties;
  • an array, a List<T> or anything that is IEnumerable<T> is a LIST of its elements, which can be any of these types, including collections and objects;
  • a Dictionary<TKey, TValue> or any IDictionary<TKey, TValue> or IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey, TValue> is a MAP; its keys are never null.

The attributes of a property that is a collection or dictionary apply to what it holds: ParquetDecimalAttribute to its decimals, ParquetEncodingAttribute to all its columns. Types that merely implement a few interfaces are guessed at only when their elements are clear; a type that contains itself, TimeSpan and the other types of the .NET libraries, multi-dimensional arrays and collections that are structs are a NotSupportedException that names the property.

Reading takes the columns of a file by the names of the properties (or of ParquetColumnAttribute; a name that differs only by case also fits when there is just one such column) and reads nothing else, so a row type can be a projection of a wider file. A column the file lacks leaves a property that can hold null at null; for any other property it is a SchemaMismatchException, as is a column stored as a type the property cannot hold. A type with a constructor that takes nothing is created and its properties with a public setter (including init-only) are set; otherwise a public constructor whose parameters are properties is used, as for a record. The same goes for nested objects, and collections are created as the property asks (an array, a List<T>, a HashSet<T>, or any type that has a public constructor without parameters and is an ICollection<T>; an interface they implement gets a list or a set) and so are dictionaries (a Dictionary<TKey, TValue> or any type that is an IDictionary<TKey, TValue> with such a constructor). The standard LIST and MAP layouts and the older layouts of lists are read.

The rows go into row groups of RowGroupSize rows, each encoded and written to the stream when it is full. The stream is not closed, and holds a partial file if serializing fails.

Remarks

The columns of a row group that the row type needs are read into memory when the first of its rows is asked for, so the memory is that of a row group, not of the file. The file is opened, and the rows can fail to match its schema, when the first row is asked for. Columns of the file that the row type has no property for are never read.

SerializeAsync<TRow>(IEnumerable<TRow>, Stream, ParquetSerializerOptions?, CancellationToken)

Writes the rows to the stream as a Parquet file, without blocking while the stream is written. A row group is encoded while the one before is being written, so the time is that of the slower of the two instead of both, and no more than two row groups are held in memory.
